Court No. - 21
Case :- Writ - C No. - 50082 of 2011
Petitioner :- Bijendra Singh And Others

Respondent :- State of U.P. and Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Anil Kumar Shukla,Smt. Sarita Shukla

Counsel for Respondent :- Akhilesh Kumar Sharma,Suresh Singh
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
Civil Misc. Withdrawal Application No. 5 of 2024.
1.
Heard Smt. Sarita Shukla, learned counsel for the applicants/petitioners.

She submits that the petitioners no. 6 and 9 are willing to receive compensation and therefore, the writ petition in respect Bijendra Singh And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68051151/
1 of the petitioners no. 6 and 9, be also dismissed as withdrawn.
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The application is allowed.
3. The writ petition stands dismissed as withdrawn on behalf of petitioners no. 6 and 9.
Order on Writ Petition 4.

The writ petition on behalf of petitioners no. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 has already been dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 17.10.2022.
5.

The writ petition is now pending consideration only on behalf of petitioners no. 7 and 8.
6.

The petitioners have prayed for quashing of the Notifications dated 26.02.2009 and 19.02.2010 issued under Section 4 r/w Section 17 (4) and Section 6 r/w Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in respect of 246.2360 hectare of land of Village-Parsol, Pargana-Dankaur, Tehsil-Sadar,
District-Gautam Budh Nagar.
7. The acquisition was for planned development in district Gautam Budh Nagar through Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority.

As a large parcel of land was needed for development of the entire area as an integrated township and therefore, 21 different notifications covering 14 villages were issued, the details of which are as follows:
Sl. No. Village Name Notification u/s 4(1)17 Date Notification u/s 6/17 Date 1.
Dungarpur Reelka 3080-77-3-10-38 Arjan/10 Date 02-12-2010 495-77-3-11-38 Arjan/10 Date 24.03.2011 2. Rustampur 605-77-3-2009-30 Arjan/09 Date 20.02.2009 596-77-3-2010-30 Arjan/09 Date 26.02.2010 3.

entities.text: Bijendra Singh And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The main ground of attack is that dispensation of inquiry under Section 5A was illegal.

9. Sri Manish Goyal, learned Additional Advocate General assisted by Sri Abhay Pratap Singh,
appearing for the respondent-Authority (YEIDA) points out that all the nine set of notifications were subject matter of challenge in different writ petitions before this Court and the challenge was repelled, against which the land holders filed various SLPs before the Supreme Court.
10. He further submits that in some cases challenge was accepted and the writ petitions were allowed.
YEIDA filed review applications which were rejected and aggrieved thereby it went up in SLP before the Supreme Court.

entities.text: Kali Charan and Others vs. State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Shyoraj Singh v. State of U.P (Writ-C No. 30747 of 2010)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have gone through the said judgement and we find the submission to be correct.

The conclusion recorded by the Supreme Court in paragraph 42 onward is as follows:-
Bijendra Singh And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68051151/
3 "... 42.

entities.text: Bijendra Singh And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court, in the cases of Savitri Devi v. State of Uttar Pradesh; (2015) 7 SCC 21, Sahara India Commercial Corporation Limited v. State of Uttar Pradesh; (2017) 11 SCC 339 and Noida Industrial Development Authority v. Ravindra Kumar; (2022) 13 SCC 468, despite holding the invocation of the urgency clause under Sections 17(1)
and 17(4) of the Act to be illegal, nonetheless upheld the acquisition proceedings and directed enhancement of compensation so as to compensate the land owners.

entities.text: Savitri Devi v. State of Uttar Pradesh; (2015) 7 SCC 21
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sahara India Commercial Corporation Limited v. State of Uttar Pradesh; (2017) 11 SCC 339
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Noida Industrial Development Authority v. Ravindra Kumar; (2022) 13 SCC 468
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in the present case, we have concluded that the action of the State in invocation of the urgency clause is in consonance with the law.

43. The Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court, while delivering its decision in Kamal Sharma has already granted additional compensation of 64.7% to the landowners, to be offered as 'No Litigation Bonus' in consonance with the Government order dated 4th November, 2015, thus there is no scope to direct further enhancement in compensation.

44. In light of the Government order dated 4th November, 2015 and the precedents set in Savitri Devi v. State of Uttar Pradesh; (supra) and Yamuna Expressway Industrial Authority v. Shakuntla Education and Welfare Society; 2022 SCC OnLine SC 655, it is directed that 64.7% enhancement in compensation shall apply in rem,
ensuring uniform benefits to all affected landowners under the present land acquisition.

entities.text: Savitri Devi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Yamuna Expressway Industrial Authority v. Shakuntla Education and Welfare Society; 2022 SCC OnLine SC 655
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
45. The question of non-issuance of the final award and its effect on the acquisition is left open ensuring that any affected party would retain the right to challenge or seek appropriate remedy on this specific issue independently, in accordance with law.
46.
As a result of the above discussion, the appeals filed by the landowners i.e. Batch No. 1, are dismissed, and the appeals filed by YEIDA i.e. Batch No. 2, are hereby allowed. ..."

11. In view of the above, we are of the opinion that the instant case is fully covered by the judgement of the Supreme Court, accordingly, the challenge to the impugned notifications is held to be unsustainable.
12. However, in terms of paragraph 45 of the judgement of the Supreme Court in Kali Charan (Supra), liberty is reserved in favour of the petitioners to challenge the award in independent proceedings.
13. Accordingly, the petition and pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.
